issue: Inconsistent naming: 73 raw values mix spelling variants of the same company, company+drug compounds and channel tags (_MEDSCAPE, _MDALERT, _ZS, _BA, _EA).
proposed_fix: Map every raw value to three clean columns: company (standardized name), product (drug name if present) and channel_tag. Keep brand_raw for auditing. Group companies with fewer than 5 rows as OTHER when encoding.

issue: No nulls and consistent casing, but two categories are singletons (CONDITION MESSAGE, DIRECT MAIL), which cannot be learned reliably.
proposed_fix: Keep values as is. Group categories with fewer than 5 rows into 'OTHER' only in the encoded modeling file.

issue: Part of a 56-row block where country and pillar are missing together with Emma's targeting fields (mostly EMAIL ALERT). Missingness is structural, not random.
proposed_fix: Fill with an explicit 'unknown' category and add a targeting_info_missing flag so models can learn from the pattern.

issue: 56 nulls (13.4%). Values are lowercase ISO-3 codes (usa, zaf, vgb, vir...) with no readable names.
proposed_fix: Fill nulls with 'UNKNOWN', convert codes to uppercase ISO-3 and add a country_name column.

issue: Sparse categories: vnm and ind (3 rows each), zmb (4) and zwe (5) are too small to model on their own.
proposed_fix: Group countries with fewer than 10 rows into 'OTHER' in the encoded file.

issue: 56 nulls (same rows as the missing country block). 'other' has only 2 rows.
proposed_fix: Fill nulls with 'unknown'. Keep 'other' as is and let it fall into the rare bucket during encoding.

issue: Part of the same 56-row block: media_type, profession and specialty are missing on the same rows as country and pillar. Missingness is structural, not random.
proposed_fix: Fill with an explicit 'unknown' category. Covered by the same targeting_info_missing flag.

issue: 80 nulls: 56 from the missing block plus 24 more on LILLY, MERCK and NOVARTIS rows that otherwise have full targeting data.
proposed_fix: Fill with 'unknown' and lowercase values (editorial_videos, sponsored_videos).

issue: Mixed data types: numeric codes (8, 99, 10-23) sit in the same column as text labels (psychologist, physician assistant, physician). Codes have no lookup table.
proposed_fix: Treat every value as a category label (code_8, code_99, psychologist...). Codes are nominal, not ordinal, so they must never be used as numbers. Ask WebMD for the code dictionary.

issue: 56 nulls (all inside the 56-row block).
proposed_fix: Fill with 'unknown'.

issue: Implausible pairings: psychologist paired with urology specialty.
proposed_fix: Keep the rows but note the pairing to WebMD. Do not build features that depend on profession x specialty combinations.

issue: 'undefined' is a hidden null. Together with real nulls, 84% of rows carry no specialty information.
proposed_fix: Convert 'undefined' and nulls to 'unknown' and add a has_specialty flag. Use npi_specialty (100% filled) as the main specialty feature.

issue: Mixed types again: numeric codes (32, 35, 45, 59, 70, 77) alongside text.
proposed_fix: Store as string labels (code_77 etc.), never as numbers.

issue: Dates are stored as text with a ' UTC' suffix instead of a datetime type. 3 rows are null.
proposed_fix: Parse to datetime. Impute the 3 nulls with the median start date for the same company and add a start_date_imputed flag. Derive start_year, start_quarter, start_month and campaign_age_days.

issue: 414 rows (99.3%) use the placeholder 2099-12-31 23:59:59, and the other 3 are null. There is no real end date anywhere, so duration cannot be computed.
proposed_fix: Drop the column. It carries no information (it is effectively constant). Use start-date features instead.

issue: Strong right skew (skew 3.3 to 5.8) with 55 IQR outliers in the worst column. A handful of very large campaigns dominate.
proposed_fix: Keep the rows (they are real campaigns, not errors). Add log1p versions of each column for modeling.

issue: Milestone plan expected this column to be 100% null, but in this file it has 0 nulls and passes all consistency checks.
proposed_fix: No drop needed. Confirm the file version with our coach so the team is aligned.

issue: Budget does not match cpe x engagements: 2 rows have $0 budget and 5 more have near-zero budgets (under $300) for hundreds of engagements.
proposed_fix: Keep the rows but add a budget_anomaly flag so they can be excluded from cost-efficiency analysis.

issue: Leakage for the CPE target: cpe = total_budget_spent / total_engagements, so a model given both columns can calculate CPE directly. For the total_spend target they are fair inputs (budget is planned before the campaign and is the strongest single predictor of spend, log correlation 0.84).
proposed_fix: Use both as features for total_spend. When predicting CPE, leave out total_budget_spent (and its log) so the model cannot rebuild the answer.

issue: Checked against unique_engaged_hcps / unique_reach: 0 mismatches. No issue.
proposed_fix: No action.

issue: No nulls. engagement_frequency matches its formula. pre_avg_NRx = pre_NRx / n_periods with a consistent divisor. Moderate skew only.
proposed_fix: No cleaning needed. Optionally add n_periods = pre_NRx / pre_avg_NRx as a feature.

issue: Measured after the campaign, so it is not known when H2 budgets are being planned. Using it as an input would give the model information it will not have in practice.
proposed_fix: Keep in cleaned_df for EDA and the prescription-lift story, but exclude from the feature sets for total_spend and CPE.

issue: Post-campaign value (post_NRx / n_periods). Not known at planning time, same as post_NRx.
proposed_fix: Keep for EDA, exclude from the feature sets for total_spend and CPE.

issue: Two columns with almost the same name hold different values (correlation 0.78). pre_avg_NRx follows a clear formula; pre_NRx_avg does not, and its definition is undocumented.
proposed_fix: Keep both for now, flag for WebMD to define pre_NRx_avg. Avoid putting both in the same model until the meaning is confirmed.

issue: One value uses a different format with a numeric code: '3320 - Anesthesiologists'. All other values are plain specialty names.
proposed_fix: Rename to 'Anesthesiology' to match the rest of the column.

issue: Mixed taxonomies: US Census divisions (South Atlantic, Mid-Atlantic, Mountain, West South Central) sit next to informal regions (Southeast, Southwest, West, Midwest) that overlap them. 'West South Central' is a singleton.
proposed_fix: Map 'West South Central' to 'Southwest' (its largest state is Texas). Keep the other labels, and note the overlap for WebMD.

issue: US regions are assigned to non-US countries (South Africa, India, Vietnam, Zambia, Zimbabwe, Virgin Islands). Region likely describes the HCP audience, not the country, but this is unconfirmed.
proposed_fix: Keep both columns and add a region_country_mismatch flag. Ask WebMD what region represents.

issue: Rounding differences of +/-0.01 against post_NRx - pre_NRx. No real error.
proposed_fix: No action. Use the provided NRx_lift column as is for EDA. It is post-campaign, so it stays out of the feature sets.

issue: Matches NRx_lift / pre_NRx exactly. 4 rows differ slightly from (post-pre)/pre because of the rounding in NRx_lift.
proposed_fix: No action. Post-campaign, so keep for EDA and the business story but out of the feature sets.

issue: 93 nulls (22.3%). cpe is fixed per product (BRAND ALERT 39, EMAIL ALERT 3, BRANDSPOT 68) and missing for every other product. Budget / engagements shows the true value is 39 for 92 of the 93 rows.
proposed_fix: Impute cpe = total_budget_spent / total_engagements (rounded to 2 decimals) and add a cpe_imputed flag.

issue: As a target, known cpe is a fixed rate per product, so sub_product_name predicts it perfectly. The overview asks for meta_mapped_cpe, which is not in this file.
proposed_fix: Confirm with the Challenge Advisor whether cpe is the intended CPE target or whether meta_mapped_cpe will be provided. Until then, treat total_spend as the main target.

issue: 3 nulls in the primary target (the same 3 rows missing campaign dates). Rebuilding them from actual_spend_per_engagement x total_engagements gives exactly the column median, so the source had already median-filled them. Their true spend is unknown.
proposed_fix: Fill with the rebuilt value so the file has no blanks, add a total_spend_imputed flag, and exclude these 3 rows from training and evaluation when total_spend is the target.

issue: 8 rows have total_spend under 1,000, including 2 at exactly 0. MAPE is undefined at 0 and explodes near 0, which would distort the headline metric.
proposed_fix: Add a spend_near_zero flag. Exclude these rows when calculating MAPE (report how many were excluded) and model log1p(total_spend) to handle the wide range.

issue: Extreme range (0 to about 39 billion, skew 6.0). total_spend is also a median of about 1,800x total_budget_spent, so the two columns measure different things. The overview confirms spend runs from near zero to billions, but the difference from budget is not documented.
proposed_fix: Model the log of total_spend and convert predictions back for MAPE. Ask WebMD how total_spend differs from total_budget_spent.

issue: Leakage for the primary target: actual_spend_per_engagement = total_spend / total_engagements and spend_per_NRx_lift = total_spend / NRx_lift. Either one lets a model rebuild total_spend almost exactly. (Separately, 2 rows are off from the formula only through rounding, and 2 are zero.)
proposed_fix: Keep in cleaned_df for EDA, but never use these columns (or their logs) as features for total_spend or CPE.
